summary: When a purple worm digests a nurse corpse dropped into the swallowed state, do.c:engulfer_digests_food() heals the swallower and calls muse.c:mcureblindness(mon, FALSE). JavaScript already ports mcureblindness(), but the digestion branch leaves it as note_unported(), so the worm remains blind. The next stethoscope status line incorrectly says “blind, digesting you” instead of “digesting you”; the later monster attack then diverges because its sight flag was not restored. Wire the existing helper at the source call.

source.branch: dropz() handles an item while u.uswallow is true. For a digesting holder and a corpse whose species is PM_NURSE, engulfer_digests_food() prints the digestion message, calls healmon(u.ustuck, u.ustuck->mhpmax, 0), then calls mcureblindness(u.ustuck, FALSE) before deleting the corpse. The cure helper clears mcansee and mblinded state only when the monster is currently unable to see; with verbos false it emits no message.
dependencies: muse.c:mcureblindness is already implemented in js/muse.js and already wired from potion.c, zap.c, and muse.c callers.

evidence: The selected v66 manifest and recording identities match the saved queue: manifest SHA256 4cb5635d3288024bb20bcec606b739b01242610f3342409d90110a6dd390378c, recording SHA256 eee8667d4ae1f1afde080e1c91ee31fbcde0df175b9b98ea169d22c5a3f398df. The immutable C recording shows the partly eaten nurse corpse dropped at segment 0 step 531, “The corpse is instantly digested!” at step 532, and “Your movements are now unencumbered. You can see again.” at step 533.

Upstream do.c:849-882 sets could_heal for PM_NURSE, heals the purple worm, and calls mcureblindness(u.ustuck, FALSE) before delobj(). Upstream muse.c:2872-2881 sets mcansee=1 and mblinded=0; the FALSE verbosity argument suppresses the visible cure message.

The JavaScript do.js:2281-2329 mirrors the nurse corpse branch and healmon call but currently records note_unported("mon.c mcureblindness") rather than calling the existing helper. The helper is exported as mcureblindness() in js/muse.js:734 and has the matching mcansee/mblinded updates.

Fresh bounded replay of this exact admitted recording at worker HEAD 3ad0638e710ad8071386f7646b55aa34bcb606b6 (run-2wQM3J) emits all 621 screens and reproduces the first screen mismatch at step 554, key u: C row 1 column 0 is “d”, JS is “b”. C shows “digesting you”; replaying the same prefix through step 554 shows JS text “blind, digesting you” and the purple worm state has mblinded=98 and mcansee=false. The C line omits the blind clause after the step-532 nurse cure.

The same replay reports the first RNG mismatch later at step 578: C rnd(20)=11 in mhitu.c:mattacku(), while JS begins with rn2(4)=2. This follows the skipped source cure and the persistent blind state; it is not evidence of an independent attack owner. The existing saved queue baseline records 44 screens remaining, 2757/2774 RNG calls, and its first later combat difference in mattacku().

insight.c:mstatusline() appends “, blind” exactly when mblinded is nonzero or mcansee is false, then appends “, digesting you” for a swallowed purple worm. Its emitted status line therefore exposes the stale monster state without changing it; the causal missing update is the discarded mcureblindness call in do.c:engulfer_digests_food().
